title: refactor: unify autorollback engine and stabilize canary/AB/shadow workflows
author: Avery Patel
description: Motivation: our autorollback logic and workflow orchestration for canary, A/B and shadow traffic have diverged over time. This causes duplicated logic, inconsistent observability, and occasional race conditions during staged rollouts. This PR refactors the autorollback engine into a single reusable core, adds explicit stability guards for staged shadow and canary sequences, and improves observability and e2e tests. High-level changes included: - unified autorollback core with plugin hooks for rollout strategies - metric quorum and composite-metric support for multi-signal rollbacks - explicit quarantine/probing stage APIs for shadow traffic - clearer telemetry with grouped rollback reasons and per-route time-series - e2e tests that run realistic canary AB and shadow sequences against the canary harness - docs and migration notes for rollout policies Checklist: - [x] Implement unified autorollback core - [x] Migrate existing canary and AB workflows to use core - [x] Add staged shadow/quarantine API and safety guards - [x] Add composite metric quorum and optional metric weighting - [x] Add e2e tests (perf-canary harness) - [x] Update docs and rollout policy schema - [x] Run CI and fix lint/flake failures Related: Linear ENG-4822, PM-317. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4822/unified-rollouts-design Notes: This description is a single continuous string containing the sections above.
commits_summary: 4 commits: refactor autorollback core; add composite-metric quorum; staged shadow/quarantine APIs; e2e tests + docs
changed_files: services/rollouts/autorollback_core.py - new core, state machine and plugin hooks
services/rollouts/scheduler.py - integrate unified core with existing scheduler and add stability guards
api/v2/rollouts.go - expose stagedShadow/quarantine endpoints and policy validation
console/rollouts/telemetry.js - rollup telemetry and clearer rollback reason tags
perf-canary/tests/e2e_canary_workflow.py - new e2e scenarios (canary, AB, shadow)
docs/rollouts/policy-schema.yaml - added compositeMetric, quorum and stabilityGuard fields
ci/workflows/rollouts-e2e.yml - added e2e job that runs against perf-canary harness
observability/alerts/rollout-alerts.yaml - tune alerts for quorum failures
README.md - top-level note about migration and opt-in flag
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (reviewer): Left a comment: 'Nice cleanup — two concerns: 1) metric quorum defaults could be surprising, we should default to conservative behavior and 2) scheduler integration needs a per-route backoff to avoid thundering re-rollouts.'

Avery Patel (author): Reply: 'Agree on conservative defaults. Updated docs and schema to require explicit quorum opt-in and default to single-metric behavior. Added per-route exponential backoff in scheduler (configurable).'
Marisol Gomez (reviewer): Left a comment: 'e2e tests look flaky locally for the staged shadow probe on noisy telemetry. Added a suggested change to increase probe window and add retries.'
Avery Patel (author): Reply: 'Increased probe window and added retry with jitter; updated test harness. CI passed after change.'
Ravi Singh (approver): 'Approving — good coverage and migration path. Recommend follow-up on observability dashboards (tracked in ENG-4870).'
CI Bot: 'All checks passed after final push.'
release_notes:
- Refactor autorollback into a unified core with plugin hooks
- Add composite-metric quorum support for multi-signal rollbacks (opt-in)
- Introduce staged shadow / quarantine APIs and stability guards
- Improved telemetry and rollback reason tagging
- e2e tests for canary, A/B and shadow workflows
Migration: opt-in migration helper script included; no automatic changes to existing policies.
testing_notes: Canary and AB sequences validated against perf-canary harness. Observed stable behavior across 50 runs with quorum set to majority; staged shadow probe reduced false positives by ~60% when probe window increased. No regression in throughput observed in dedicated clusters.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: refactor is internal and behind opt-in flags for policy migration. Major risk relates to misconfigured quorum settings causing delayed rollbacks; mitigated by conservative defaults and prominent docs. Follow-up (ENG-4870) will add rollout dashboards and alert runbooks.
